newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods flatten in late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods flatten in late trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices were unchanged late Wednesday, after easing early on weak demand, traders said.
Demand fell as severe flooding in the north half of California kept motorists away from roads.
CARB-grade gasoline in San Francisco remained about two cents under Los Angeles, at 77/78 cents a gallon. L.A. material held at its early levels of 79/80, a cent under Tuesday.
Premium grades in both markets was four cents higher.
With demand weak, sellers dominated the market with offers, traders said.
Meanwhile, jet fuel eased in anticipation of imports. The product had risen earlier this week as supplies were diverted into the production of winter-grade diesel fuel, brokers said.
